chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The most superior of charities is a charity that comes from the surplus of the hand.'

key_terms.فَضْلِ الْكَفِّ: Surplus of the hand (excess wealth beyond needs)

ai.seo_question: What is the best type of charity according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith emphasizes the virtue of discretionary charity (sadaqat al-fadl) over obligatory alms, reflecting the Shia emphasis on voluntary piety. The phrase 'surplus of the hand' signifies wealth remaining after fulfilling one's own and dependents' essential needs, a concept often linked to the practice of giving from the best of one's possessions as highlighted in Shia exegesis.
